question.leadin: Name these American generals from World War II.
question.text: The U.S. Army's chief of staff during the war was this man, who served as Harry Truman's Secretary of State and earned a Nobel Peace Prize for his "European Recovery" plan to repair the war's damage.
question.clue: Another king with this name went against the advice of his ministers and refused to grant asylum to the czar of Russia, even though they were cousins.

swap.text: Name this technology. Al Gore was misquoted as saying he "invented" this technology in a CNN interview, when in reality he was referring to his support of the High Performance Computing Act.

question.leadin: Give the following about containment, the official US policy for stopping the spread of communism.
question.text: This President, who served between Ford and Reagan, tried to shift from containment to a more pacifist foreign policy until the Soviets invaded Afghanistan in 1979. He won a Nobel Peace Prize in 2002, in part for his work with Habitat for Humanity.
question.clue: This President lost his reelection bid in a race that featured Independent candidate John B. Anderson.

question.clue: This event, which shared its name with a French protectorate, began when the USS Maddox fired warning shots at torpedo boats commanded by Le Duy Khoai.

question.text: Name this target of an attack by Joseph Welch.

question.leadin: Answer the following about underappreciated female scientists in American History.
question.text: The film Hidden Figures chronicles the contributions of Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan, and Mary Jackson to this NASA project. As part of this mission, Alan Shepard became the first American in space.
question.clue: The number 7 featured in the names of every vehicle used, including Friendship 7, flown by John Glenn, and Freedom 7, flown by Alan Shepard, the first American in space.

swap.leadin: Answer each of the following about the Saturday Night Massacre.
swap.text: The Saturday Night Massacre was touched off by Richard Nixon ordering the firing of the independent prosecutor investigating the cover up of a break-in at this Washington, D.C. hotel, which led to several resignations and one firing.
swap.clue: Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward reported on the events in this building.

question.leadin: The United States' judicial system has seen plenty of odd defenses used by defendants. answer some questions about them.
question.text: This defense was used by Dan White after the murders of Harvey Milk and George Moscone. His lawyers argued that he suffered from depression caused by a change in diet to the namesake sugary treat.

question.text: Name this National Security Advisor who proposed the advent of the "Technetronic Era" and wrote books like The Grand Chessboard.
